decisions.id: D10 (amendment 1, round 2: the cascade wire after a ruling)
decisions.summary: the cascade wire stays live after ANY ruling: the trigger id advances on every cascade ruling (cascade@<rulings + 1>), and the wire fires again only when CASCADE_MIN (10) further dispatches since the last ruling find the ratio still past 1.0 - after a continue or an accept alike (hm_arbiter.cascade / cascade_state)
decisions.why: Round 1's block answered in the form it allowed. A quiet stretch after a ruling, in which the ratio is past the threshold but the wire does not fire, narrows FR-010's literal 'the cascade ratio passing a set threshold'; it is implied by the spec's own words, because FR-011 makes one ruling per trigger binding and 'continue' means 'one more round', so a fixed bar would re-trip on the very next dispatch. Round 1 offered two forms (the bar raised to the ratio at the ruling, or a stated step) and the plan takes the second: a stated step of CASCADE_MIN dispatches, the floor measured from the SC-006 replay (m:cascade-threshold, fewest_dispatches 10; its four windows re-run this round from the transcript: 84/193 0.44, 55/409 0.13, 23/17 1.35, 16/27 0.59, all as recorded), with the ratio's threshold left fixed at 1.0. Both faults round 1 found are gone. (1) Size: at wave 108's base the wire trips at dispatch 18 and, after a continue, again at 28 - ten more, about one and a half of 0105's 5-7-check rounds and no longer a whole threshold's worth (17 there, 409 at wave 106's base); since the cascade is feature-wide, a round there is several units' checks, so ten is a fair reading of 'one more round', and the per-unit round cap still fires on its own. (2) An accept or process-fault no longer switches the wire off: cascade_state advances the id on every ruling, so trip() writes a fresh trigger. tests/tooling/test_hm_arbiter.py test_the_cascade_wire_stays_live_after_any_ruling pins the accept case (cascade@2 after an accept, live again ten dispatches later); test_replays_375.py re-run this round: 2 passed. The 'last' count is taken at the trip, not at the ruling; a dispatch let through by ARBITER_OK in between only makes the re-trip come sooner, the safe side. decisions.id: D58a (the start = the later of the first event and the latest reopening)
decisions.summary: feature_start returns max(first event in the clone, most recent closed->open commit time); a reopening older than the first event leaves the first event
decisions.why: FR-042 makes the reopening the start; taking the later only ever delays the hour. Applied literally where the reopening predates this clone's first event (a reopening committed in another clone hours earlier), the hour has already passed at the first event and the glyph check fires at once - the very thing the GM said he does not like. Literal application defeats the request's stated purpose; amendment 9's 'start in the clone' is kept.

decisions.id: D58b (the state read over the whole directory by hm_approval._state_at)
decisions.summary: each commit's state and its parent's read by hm_approval._state_at itself (every file ls-tree lists under specs/<f> at that revision, then speckit-todo.feature()); the walk is git log -- specs/<f>; 'closed' and 'done - GM review pending' both count as closed; T59 adds a GM-review-pending close-and-reopen fixture
decisions.why: Round 1's finding resolved: _state_at (scripts/hooks/lib/hm_approval.py:229) writes every file of specs/<d> at the revision before calling todo.feature(), so gm_rows, holding and lands_open_ids are seen and 335/378's 'done - GM review pending' is reachable; the walk now covers the files that move the state, and the fixture pins the case. Counting a GM-pending close as closed is what the GM's 'reopened features' covers and what D54 already does, and only ever moves the hour later, which is the request.

decisions.id: D58c (the 200-commit bound)
decisions.summary: the walk stops at 200 commits of the directory; past it the first event stands
decisions.why: The outcome differs only when the latest reopening is more than 200 directory commits back AND under an hour old. Measured 2026-10-12 (every specs/*/ directory, git log --format=%ct, densest 60-minute window): at most 57 commits to one directory in any hour (271), so 200 within an hour has never happened and the bound cannot cut a reopening still inside its hour. The plan's stated counts are wrong for what they label, though: 83 (375) and 293 (328) are the spec.md+tasks.md counts; over the whole directory, which is what the walk now reads, they are 137 and 476 (same date and method). Correct the parenthetical (and the 'can only cut ... long past its hour' reasoning should rest on the per-hour density, not on totals); the ruling does not rest on it.

decisions.id: D58d (the answer kept in glyph-clock.json)
decisions.summary: the reopening found is cached under the feature, keyed by the newest commit of specs/<f>, reused while that commit is unchanged; tested
decisions.why: A means of not re-walking history on every stop-hook turn; a reopening exists only as a commit to the directory, so any new one changes the key and the answer is never stale. It decides nothing FR-042 settles.
